newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dust settles as Australian bond futures rollover.
newsitem.headline: Dust settles as Australian bond futures rollover.

text.p: Australian bond yields crept above their initial lows after the dust settled following Monday's midday close out of the June three- and 10-year bond futures contracts.
The market got off to a flying start following a rally in futures in after-hours trading late on Friday, which tracked an advance in U.S. Treasuries on a weak PPI for May.

"The PPI data, together with other weaker data over recent weeks, confirms our view that the Fed is unlikely to tighten at the July 1-2 FOMC meeting," said David Bassanese, senior economist at Bankers Trust Australia.

If the Fed does refrain from tightening it will likely fuel already bullish expectations for a further easing in local monetary policy if the Reserve Bank has not already loosened by the time of the next monthly RBA board meeting on July 1.

Local yields dived last week following an extremely weak labour force report, which combined with other soft data in recent weeks is expected to see a cut in current 5.5 percent official rates before too long.
September bill futures are practically discounting a 50 basis point easing already, touching a contract high of 94.94 in early trading and equating to a cash rate of 5.06 percent.

Ten-year bond yields sank to their lowest level since February 1994 and below 7.0 percent following the advance in the now-expired June contract to a peak of 93.090, overtaking the most recent peak of 93.015 last December.
However, with the new front position September having been trading at a discount to June, the contract is expected to find 93.015 a resistance level again.

There is very little on the data calendar this week, leaving the market focussed on the data flow in the U.S., which on Tuesday alone sees CPI, housing starts, industrial pruduction and capacity utilization for May.

The local market reversed its initial outperformance against the dollar bloc as yields gave up some of their initial decline. The Australian/U.S. 10-year spread had breached 50 basis points in early trading. The short end of the Canadian curve outperformed on lessening concerns of a U.S. tightening.
